style.vernacular: Brick-and-glass lakeside metropolis: Victorian bay-and-gable and Georgian red-brick houses downtown, post-war brick bungalows and slab towers in the suburbs, pink sandstone and limestone for institutions, big-box malls and campuses ringed by car parks in Scarborough, North York and Etobicoke, and glass condo and office towers. Pitched asphalt-shingle roofs, flat membrane roofs on commercial buildings, broadleaf street trees with conifers, and ravine parkland.
style.ornament: Victorian bay-and-gable timber bargeboards and brick polychrome bands; Georgian and Regency symmetry on early houses; Queenston and Credit-valley sandstone and limestone on civic buildings; International Style black and glass towers; strip-mall signage fascias.

sources.what: bay-and-gable houses, red brick default, pinkish Credit River sandstone, limestone civic buildings, post-war brick slab towers, glazed condo towers, concrete and aluminium modern landmarks
